sentences.text: The contention of learned counsel for the revisionist is that no offence against the revisionist is disclosed and the present prosecution has been instituted with a malafide intention for the purpose of harassment.
He pointed out certain documents and statements in support of his contention.
It is further contended that the revisionist is a poor street vendor.
The compliance of Section 46(4) of Food Safety and Standard Act has not been followed and sample has not been verified by the laboratory for re-examination.
It is also contended that nothing has been found noxious or spurious and only sub-standard was found less than the prescribed limit of 10% and it was found 5.68%.

Thereafter the revisionist filed a Civil Appeal (F.S.S.Act) No.18 of 2018, before the Court below,
which was partly allowed by reducing the amount of fine imposed fine from Rs.2.00 lass to Rs.80,000/-.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the Court is of the view that the amount of fine of Rs.80,000/- imposed upon the revisionist by the court below should be reduced to Rs.40,000/-
and as such it is directed that the revisionist shall deposit Rs.40,000/- before the court below within a period of one month from today.

If the revisionist does not deposit Rs.40,000/ within the aforesaid period, the benefit of this order shall not be available to the revisionist and the court below shall be at liberty to take coercive action against the revisionist.
The appellate order dated 14.8.2019 is modified to that extent .
With the above observations/direction, present revision is finally disposed off.

Order Date :- 24.10.2019/IA  Ittefaaq Ahmad vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147374736/
